L264: From the L TOA_5m airborne radiances and the L TOA_Xm

L429: 4. RESULTS & DISCUSSION
L430: 
L431: 4.1 Sensitivity to atmospheric effects
L432: A PLSR model was built from each of the images at 5m:
L433: 
L434: 5m_AISA and 5m_HYPXIM. The best model was obtained
L435: 
L436: from the AISA airborne image (R²val ≈ 0.75). Nevertheless,
L437: 
L438: the performance of the model obtained from the satellite
L439: 
L440: simulated data at 5m is only slightly less accurate (R²val ≈
L441: 
L442: 0.71). So the atmosphere seems to slightly impact the
L443: 
L444: performances of the PLSR-based prediction models.
L445: 
L446: Both PLSR models built from the spectra of the
L447: 
L448: 5m_AISA and 5m_HYPXIM images were applied to the
L449: entire 5m_AISA and 5m_HYPXIM images respectively, in
L450: 
L451: order to obtain predicted clay content maps (Figure 2).
L452: 
L453: No significant difference can be observed on these
L454: 
L455: maps by visual inspection. The same large pedological units
L456: 
L457: can be identified, so same relative predictions have been
L458: 
L459: made by both PLSR models. Contrasted values and soil
L460: 
L461: patterns appears between the Pliocene area, located in the
L462: 
L463: southeast corner of the image, and the Miocene area,
L464: 
L465: covering the rest of the image. Pliocene area exhibits low
L466: and weakly variable topsoil clay contents, whereas the
L467: 
L468: Miocene area shows a large range of clay content values.
L469: 
L470: Variations within the Miocene area are also visible. They
L471: 
L472: follow the geological pattern formed by the alternating
L473: 
L474: sandstone and marl outcrops, yielding low (blue) and high
L475: 
L476: (red) values of clay content, respectively (Figure 2).
L477: 
L478: So when a correct compensation of the atmosphere
L479: 
L480: effects was done, no differences were detected between the
L481: soil property maps retrieved from airborne imagery and the
L482: 
L483: ones from spaceborne imagery.
L484: 
L485: Fig. 2. Predicted clay content maps obtained from the a)
L486: 
L487: 5m_AISA and b) 5m_HYPXIM images.

L489: 4.2 Sensitivity to degradation in image spatial resolutions
L490: 
L491: Whatever the spatial resolution from 5 to 30m, the PLSR
L492: 
L493: models built from simulated-satellite images were accurate
L494: 
L495: (RMSEC < 100 g/kg and R²c al > 0.6). Only slight differences
L496: 
L497: of prediction performance were observed from the validation
L498: dataset: the spatial resolution of 5, 15 and 30m gave similar
L499: 
L500: performance of prediction (R²val = 0.71 and RMSEP =
L501: 
L502: 90g/kg), whereas the spatial resolution of 20m provided
L503: 
L504: better performance (R²val = 0.81 and RMSEP = 73 g/kg).
L505: 
L506: The PLSR models built from simulated-satellite images at
L507: 
L508: 60 and 90 m were inaccurate with R²cal < 0.4 and RMSEC >
L509: 
L510: 130 g/kg. These low performances may be due to i) the
L511: 
L512: spectral heterogeneity and/or ii) the soil properties
L513: heterogeneity in the pixels of 60 and 90m. Indeed other soil
L514: 
L515: properties than clay (iron, organic carbon …) and/or
L516: 
L517: heterogeneity of the land surface over the pixel (differences
L518: 
L519: of ploughing, rugosity, crust…) may affect the spe ctral
L520: 
L521: response and the model performances.
L522: 
L523: These results indicate that the model performances
L524: 
L525: do not decrease linearly with the decrease of spatial
L526: 
L527: resolution as it may have been expected. Below 30 m,
L528: 
L529: performances seems not be related with resolution.
L530: Conversely model performances decrease much more than
L531: 
L532: linearly beyond 30 meters.
L533: 
L534: Each PLSR model built from 5 to 30m was applied
L535: 
L536: to its corresponding simulated-satellite image and allows
L537: 
L538: obtaining predicted clay maps. As PLSR models built from
L539: 
L540: simulated-satellite images at 60 and 90 m were inaccurate,
L541: 
L542: no predicted clay map was built at both resolutions.
L543: 
L544: Whatever the spatial resolution from 5 to 30m, no
L545: 
L546: large difference occurs in absolute prediction, considering
L547: the distribution of predicted clay content over the entire
L548: 
L549: area. The clay prediction map of the Kamech catchment
L550: 
L551: (black upper rectangle in Figure 2) from the 5m_HYPXIM
L552: 
L553: image shows a strong variation in the soil pattern on a small
L554: 
L555: scale, with a close succession of clay-rich areas and clay-
L556: 
L557: poor areas, oriented northwest/southeast, corresponding to
L558: 
L559: marl and sandstone outcrops, respectively (Figure 3a). Some
L560: 
L561: mixed areas also appear in transition areas between these
L562: outcrops and in shoal areas. The reduction in spatial
L563: 
L564: resolution resulted in a decrease in the number of bare soil
L565: 
L566: pixels that can be used in VNIR/SWIR spectrometry
L567: 
L568: providing only a partial view of the succession of clay-rich
L569: 
L570: areas and clay-poor areas. In particular, clay-rich areas with
L571: 
L572: a width less than 60 m disappears when a spatial resolution
L573: 
L574: of 30 m is used (Figure 3b).

L576: So although regression methods showed robust
L577:

L581: prediction from 15 m of spatial resolution and a loss of

L583: information on soil spatial structures from 30 m of spatial
L584: 
L585: resolution.

L593: 6. CONCLUSION
L594: 
L595: These preliminary works show that the use of PRISMA,
L596: 
L597: EnMap, Shalom or HYPXIM data may allow for soil
L598: property mapping over large areas. A future hyperspectral
L599: 
L600: spaceborne sensor with a spatial resolution at 5m would be
L601: 
L602: an excellent source of data for soil mapping. Beyond 5m, the
L603: 
L604: adequate spatial resolution may depend on the short-scale
L605: 
L606: variability of the soil property over the study filed.
L607: 
L608: As [7] showed that spatial resolution is secondary
L609: 
L610: in importance to spectral resolution to map vegetation and
L611: 
L612: bare soil, it would be interesting and important to engage
L613: next studies of the sensitivity of soil property prediction to
L614: 
L615: degradation in spectral resolutions. Moreover, to reinforce
L616: 
L617: these conclusions and the guideline, this study could be
L618: 
L619: enlarge to additional soil properties.
